platformRevenue.label: Third-party seller services net sales (commissions, fulfillment and shipping fees, and other third-party seller services)

thirdPartyUnitShare.label: WW seller unit mix: % of worldwide paid units sold by third-party sellers, Q4 2025 only (excludes Whole Foods Market)

ecosystem.notes: Amazon does not report GMV or any total value of third-party sales, so measure is null. platformRevenue is the third-party seller services net sales line (what Amazon keeps from sellers: commissions plus fulfillment and shipping fees); it excludes advertising sold to sellers (advertising services $68.635B is a separate line). The 61% unit share is a Q4 2025 quarterly figure (quarters in 2025: 61%, 62%, 62%, 61%; no full-year figure is published) and counts units, not dollars; it is read from the earnings release filed with the SEC as Exhibit 99.1 to the Form 8-K of Feb 5, 2026. Both study entries keep value null because the claims are a percentage, a per-seller average ($375,000) and a count of sellers, not billions. The 60% sales share, the $375,000 average and the 75,000 sellers above $1 million are Amazon's own self-published report (published April 2026), not an independent or commissioned study, and the 60% is stated as 'today', not as an FY2025 measurement.

taxes.notes: Taxes: us-gaap:IncomeTaxesPaidNet, net of refunds, from the income-tax note's table of cash taxes paid (U.S. federal 2,751, U.S. state 2,125, international 3,419; total 8,295 million); the supplemental cash-flow lines show the same 8,295. The 10-K says the 2025 Tax Act (accelerated depreciation, immediate expensing of domestic R&D) significantly decreased cash taxes in 2025. R&D not reported as a separate line. Amazon reports 'Technology and infrastructure' expense (108,521 million in 2025), which the 10-K says includes payroll for employees involved in research and development alongside store maintenance, AWS infrastructure and other costs; the filing does not call the line R&D, so it is not recorded.

paidout.notes: Capex is gross "Purchases of property and equipment" (131,819); the cash-flow statement also shows 3,499 of proceeds from property and equipment sales and incentives, which are not netted. Equipment acquired under finance leases (non-cash, 2,911 in 2025) is excluded. Interest and income taxes paid are inside operating cash flow, so they are not added. Not a marketplace for salesEnabled: Amazon does not disclose third-party GMV.

source.quote: The 2025 annual total compensation of our median compensated employee (identified from all full- and part-time permanent and temporary employees worldwide, excluding our CEO) was $40,206

pay.notes: Employees: a year-end count of full-time and part-time employees; the 10-K says Amazon also uses independent contractors and temporary personnel, who are not counted. Payroll: the FY2025 10-K discloses no total staff cost (payroll sits inside cost of sales, fulfillment, technology and infrastructure and other expense lines), so the 2026 proxy's CEO pay ratio median is used. It is the worldwide median for 2025, identified from all full- and part-time permanent and temporary employees as of October 1, 2025, using salary, bonus and the grant-date fair value of restricted stock units granted in the year, with annualized pay for employees who did not work the full year (except seasonal or temporary employees). The proxy also gives a U.S. full-time median of $53,211, which is not used because it covers only part of the workforce.
